request.spec:
A button downloads the people as a CSV file: a header line name,grade,retired-from,due-total,
then one line per person in list order, retired people included, with the grade in force today,
the retired-from date or nothing, and the due-total as shown. A value holding a comma, a quote or a
line break is wrapped in double quotes, with any quote inside doubled. Lines end with a line
feed.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button downloads the people as a CSV file: a header line name,grade,retired-from,due-total,
then one line per person in list order, retired people included, with the grade in force today,
the retired-from date or nothing, and the due-total as shown. A value holding a comma, a quote or a
line break is wrapped in double quotes, with any quote inside doubled. Lines end with a line
feed.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as

data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I added an "Export people (CSV)" button (`data-testid="export-people"`), and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

The change is one new front-end file, `src/main/frontend/features/export/export.slot.tsx`; the app picks it up automatically and puts the button right below the People panel. The download is named `people-<sheet>.csv`. Nothing changed on the server or in the stored data.

**What the file contains:**
- A header line `name,grade,retired-from,due-total`.
- One line per person in the same order as the list. Retired people are always included, even when "Show retired" is off.
- The grade in force today and the retired-from date, or nothing if the person isn't retired.
- The due-total exactly as the row shows it, including `n/a`. It uses the same calculation as the due-total column, so the two can't disagree.
- A value with a comma, a quote or a line break is wrapped in double quotes, with inner quotes doubled. Every line ends with a line feed.

**One limitation:** the CSV is built in the browser from the data the screen has already loaded, not fetched fresh when you click. In practice this matches what's on screen, because every change on the page reloads the data before the button can be used again. But if another user changed the sheet since you last loaded it, the export will show your loaded version until you reload the sheet.
